FR-001.title: The product MUST allow at most one interactive Fallout Terminal desktop instance for the same operating-system login session at a time.

FR-002.title: A later desktop process MUST exit successfully before composing application services, creating a window, owning campaign state, or attempting to bind the player-server port.

FR-003.title: A later desktop launch MUST request that the active Overseer window be restored and focused when that window is available.

FR-004.title: Concurrent or near-concurrent desktop launches MUST resolve to one active instance without crashing or disrupting that instance's startup.

FR-005.title: Normal or unexpected termination of the active instance MUST release ownership so the next desktop launch can start without manual cleanup.

FR-006.title: The application identity used to coordinate launches MUST remain stable across application restarts and version upgrades.

FR-007.title: Data received from a later launch MUST be treated as untrusted and MUST NOT execute commands, navigate content, or modify application state.

FR-008.title: Informational and maintenance invocations that do not start the interactive desktop application MUST preserve their existing behavior without requiring desktop-instance ownership.

FR-009.title: Duplicate prevention and active-window reactivation MUST have the same user-visible behavior on every supported desktop operating system.

FR-010.title: Duplicate prevention MUST be enabled by default and MUST require no user configuration.

FR-011.title: All data sent from a later launch to the active instance MUST use authenticated AES-256-GCM encryption with a non-zero 32-byte key shared by every copy of the application.

FR-012.title: A later desktop process MUST terminate before application composition even when its encrypted notification cannot be delivered or decrypted.

context: area: main.go and wails_host.go application bootstrap
constraint: Wails v3 single-instance guidance and untrusted second-launch data
constraint: repository Go quality and test cleanup rules
intent: Prevent duplicate interactive Fallout Terminal instances while returning repeated launches to the active Overseer window.
expectations: Cross-user or machine-wide single-instance enforcement is out of scope.
Processing arguments or other data supplied by a later launch is out of scope.
Changing version-reporting or application-update replacement-helper behavior is out of scope.
approach: Use Wails single-instance locking with a stable identity and embedded 32-byte encryption key. Exit later processes before composition and bridge authenticated callbacks to synchronized Overseer-window activation.

decisions.decision: Use application.Options.SingleInstance with exit code zero.
decisions.why: The pinned Wails runtime already owns cross-platform locking, notification, cleanup, and later-process exit.
decisions.rejected: A custom lock file or platform-specific implementation would duplicate runtime behavior.

decisions.decision: Use com.vaulttec.fallout-terminal as the single-instance identity.
decisions.why: It is the existing stable production bundle identifier and is independent of versions and paths.
decisions.rejected: Display names, executable paths, and versioned identifiers are unstable or permit duplicates.

decisions.decision: Synchronize window binding and activation while remembering one pending activation.
decisions.why: The runtime callback executes on a background listener and may arrive before window creation.
decisions.rejected: An unsynchronized captured pointer would race and a direct host lookup would broaden coupling.

decisions.decision: Ignore second-launch payload data and provide no additional data or encryption key.
decisions.why: Only the activation signal is needed, so payload contents cannot affect state, navigation, commands, or logs.
decisions.rejected: Parsing, validating, or encrypting unused data adds complexity without product value.

decisions.decision: Supersede the earlier no-encryption choice: use a unique embedded 32-byte application key for Wails instance communication.
decisions.why: The user clarified that the notification channel must use Wails secure communication without adding credential prompts or first-run key races.
decisions.rejected: Plaintext communication and operating-system credential-store provisioning before host construction.
